topic.title: Semi-log Plots
topic.summary: Semi-log plots with a logarithmically scaled y-axis, why exponential data appear linear on them, and the linear model log_n y = (log_n b)x + log_n a that comes from y = abˣ.

lesson.title: Semi-log Plots
lesson.summary: Semi-log plots with a logarithmically scaled y-axis, why exponential data appear linear on them, and the linear model log_n y = (log_n b)x + log_n a that comes from y = abˣ.
learningGoals: 2.15.A Determine if an exponential model is appropriate by examining a semi-log plot of a data set.
2.15.B Construct the linearization of exponential data.
lesson.bigIdea: Taking a logarithm of exponential outputs turns multiplication into addition, so exponential data line up along a straight line. A straight semi-log plot is evidence for an exponential model.
lesson.context: Topic 2.6 judged models with residuals, and Topic 2.12 showed that logarithms turn products into sums. A semi-log plot combines the two ideas into a quick visual test for exponential data.

sections.title: 2.15.A · On a semi-log plot, exponential data appear linear.

blocks.text: In a semi-log plot, one of the axes is logarithmically scaled with logarithm base n, where n > 1. When the y-axis of a semi-log plot is logarithmically scaled, data or functions that demonstrate exponential characteristics will appear linear.

blocks.caption: Data from y = 2(3)ˣ and the common logarithm of each output
Semi-log plot of the data: log y against x lies on a line with slope log 3 ≈ 0.477
blocks.alt: Five points at x = 0 through 4 with heights 0.301, 0.778, 1.255, 1.732, and 2.210, lying exactly on a straight dashed line that rises about 0.477 for each unit of x.

blocks.text: If for large input values of a bivariate data set the logarithms of the output values trend linear, then transformations of an exponential function can be used to model the data set. Therefore, an advantage of semi-log plots is that the dependent variable values do not need to be transformed by a constant to reveal that transformations of an exponential function would produce an appropriate model.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam
blocks.text: An exponential model is appropriate because the semi-log plot of the data, with log y on the vertical axis, appears linear.

sections.takeaway: Linear on a semi-log plot (log of y against x) means exponential.

sections.title: 2.15.B · y = abˣ becomes the line log_n y = (log_n b)x + log_n a.

blocks.text: Techniques used to model linear functions can be applied to a semi-log graph.

For an exponential model of the form y = abˣ, the corresponding linear model for the semi-log plot is y = (log_n b)x + log_n a, where n > 0 and n ≠ 1. Specifically, the linear rate of change is log_n b, and the initial linear value is log_n a.
Here the vertical coordinate of the semi-log plot is log_n of the original output. For y = 2(3)ˣ with n = 10, the line has slope log 3 ≈ 0.477 and vertical intercept log 2 ≈ 0.301.
The process also runs backward. If a semi-log plot with base 10 has the line log y = 0.5x + 1, then log b = 0.5 and log a = 1, so b = 10^0.5 ≈ 3.162 and a = 10, and y ≈ 10(3.162)ˣ.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam
blocks.text: Taking log of both sides of y = abˣ gives log y = log a + x log b, which is linear in x with slope log b and intercept log a.

sections.takeaway: Slope = log_n b, intercept = log_n a. Undo with n^(slope) and n^(intercept).

connections.title: Product and power properties
connections.body: Topic 2.12's product and power properties are exactly what turn log (abˣ) into log a + x log b, the equation of a line.
connections.transferQuestion: Write ln (5eˣ) as a linear expression in x.
connections.feedback: ln 5 + x, a line with slope 1 and intercept ln 5.

links.label: Review the power property for logarithms

connections.title: Periodic models
connections.body: Unit 3 turns to data that repeat instead of growing, which no exponential or logarithmic model can fit and which call for sinusoidal functions.
connections.transferQuestion: Would a semi-log plot of hourly temperatures over three days look linear?
connections.feedback: No. Temperatures that rise and fall each day are periodic, not exponential.
